subject: biology
topic: Sex determination, sex-linked traits, blood groups and genetic disorders

kept.q: In human beings, each sperm cell carries either an X or a Y chromosome, while every egg cell carries only an X chromosome. If a sperm cell carrying a Y chromosome fertilises an egg, what will be the sex of the resulting offspring?
options: Cannot be determined without further information
kept.explanation: The egg always gives an X chromosome. If the sperm gives a Y chromosome, the offspring becomes XY, which is male. If the sperm had given X instead, the offspring would be XX (female).
kept.pidgin: Egg dey always carry X chromosome. If the sperm wey enter am get Y, the baby go be XY, wey be male. If e be X sperm, e for be XX, wey be female.

kept.q: Mrs Ngozi is a carrier for haemophilia with genotype X^H X^h, while her husband, Mr Eze, is normal with genotype X^H Y. What proportion of their sons is expected to be haemophiliac?
kept.explanation: Sons receive the Y chromosome from the father and an X chromosome from the mother. Since the mother is X^H X^h, half of her eggs carry X^H and half carry X^h, so half the sons will be X^h Y (haemophiliac) and half will be X^H Y (normal).
kept.pidgin: Boy pikin dey collect Y from papa and X from mama. Since mama na X^H X^h, half of her eggs get X^H, half get X^h. So half the boys go be X^h Y (get di sickness) and half go normal.

kept.q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Considering how the ABO blood group alleles are inherited, which of the following correctly states the possible blood groups of their children?
options: Only blood group A and blood group B
Only blood group AB and blood group O
Only blood group A and blood group AB
Blood group A, B, AB and O in equal proportions
kept.explanation: The AB father can pass on either the I^A or I^B allele, while the O mother can only pass on the i allele. This gives children genotypes I^A i (group A) or I^B i (group B), each at 50 percent, so AB and O are impossible in their children.
kept.pidgin: Papa wey be AB fit give I^A or I^B allele, but mama wey be O fit only give i allele. So pikin go be either I^A i (A group) or I^B i (B group), each na 50 percent. AB and O no fit come out from dis marriage.

kept.q: A baby girl is diagnosed with Turner syndrome. Cytogenetic analysis of her cells would most likely reveal which of the following chromosome complements?
options: 44 autosomes plus a single X chromosome (XO)
kept.explanation: Turner syndrome results from the loss of one X chromosome, giving a total of 45 chromosomes made up of 44 autosomes and a single X (XO), instead of the normal 44 autosomes plus XX. The other options describe different chromosomal abnormalities such as Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) or triple X syndrome (XXX).
kept.pidgin: Turner syndrome dey happen when one X chromosome miss, so the total na 45 chromosomes - 44 autosomes plus just one X (XO), instead of the normal 44 plus XX. The other options na different wahala like Klinefelter (XXY) or triple X (XXX).
